# Draft social posts: Slack for scheduling

**Pattern:** Content Generation · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers scheduling work end to end across Slack, Google Sheets, PostgreSQL and WordPress.

It moves through 20 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. Weekly Schedule
2. Stamp & Shape Post
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Build the Brief
6. Draft with AI Writer
7. Anthropic Writer Model
8. Refine with AI Editor
9. Anthropic Editor Model
10. Convert to HTML
11. Publish Draft to WordPress
12. Serialize Run Output (CSV)
13. Archive Row Snapshot
14. Stamp Completion Time
15. Persist Run Metadata
16. Fingerprint for Idempotency
17. Drop Already-Processed Items
18. Summarize Run Stats
19. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
20. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing scheduling work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Weekly Schedule → Stamp & Shape Post → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Build the Brief → Draft with AI Writer → Anthropic Writer Model → Refine with AI Editor → Anthropic Editor Model → Convert to HTML → Publish Draft to WordPress → Serialize Run Output (CSV) → Archive Row Snapshot → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Google Sheets aligned by hand for scheduling
- Scheduling work where "Stamp & Shape Post" is still a manual step before Slack
- Scheduling work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Google Sheets in step for scheduling, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Google Sheets are skipped, across all 23 nodes of this scheduling build
- A failed Slack or Google Sheets call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 23 nodes in this scheduling build
- Every scheduling run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack
- The scheduling AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 23 nodes

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Anthropic API key; Google OAuth2 / service account; Postgres connection; Slack OAuth2; WordPress credentials.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Two LLM calls, not one, because a model grading its own output rarely catches its own mistakes — a dedicated critic pass, with a different system prompt focused on gaps and tone rather than generation, catches what a single writing pass misses. Publishing lands as a **draft**, never live, so a human stays the final gate before AI-authored content goes public.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Swap the Editor Model to a different provider than the Writer Model and compare the critique quality.
2. Change the critic's system message to focus on one specific weakness, like SEO or tone.
3. Add a third pass — a fact-check chain — between the writer and the editor.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Postgres connection**
Host, port, database, user, password from your Postgres provider.
_Gotcha:_ Managed providers usually require SSL enabled in the credential's options.

**Anthropic API key**
console.anthropic.com → Settings → API Keys.
_Gotcha:_ Requires purchased credit.

**WordPress credentials**
WordPress → Users → Profile → Application Passwords → add new.
_Gotcha:_ Requires HTTPS. The regular login password will not work.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Database node cannot connect**
Cause: SSL not enabled, or the n8n server's IP is not allow-listed.
Fix: Most managed database providers require both.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your scheduling process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- PostgreSQL: connect as a role that can reach only the tables below, not as the owner.
- WordPress: an application password for a user with author rights, not an administrator account.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole scheduling payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
